conviction_note: Ten small findings net mildly positive (sum +2.7). They come from a fourth quarter in a row of beating the top of the company's own revenue guide, a crowded but covering short (17.3% of float, 9.4 days to cover), and accelerating CPG digital spend at Instacart, an IPN partner. They are offset by a 74% run since the last print, a price above every published target, put skew of +12.7 and an insider-sale cluster. This name moves on the guide (Q2'26 beat plus raised guide: +51.9%; Q1'26 beat with a weak guide: -0.6%; Q3'25: -23.7%), and the Q4 guide against an implied ~$93.4M consensus cannot be resolved from public data. So p_up sits at 52 on a 26-point absolute move, which is why the scaled number (+1.0) is well under the findings sum.
bar: Q3 2026 company guide: revenue $86-90M (midpoint $88M, +6% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $12-14M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026051867/earningsrelease63026.htm, 2026-08-03). Revenue consensus $88.4M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/IBTA) and $88.6M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBTA/earnings-forecasts, snippet only, 403 on fetch). The two agree and sit at the guide midpoint. EPS consensus disputed ($0.38 Benzinga vs $0.13 Earnings Whispers, basis unclear), so nothing is sized on EPS. FY2026 revenue consensus $353.35M (StockAnalysis/S&P, 9 analysts, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ibta/forecast/), which implies a Q4 consensus of about $93.4M (+5.5% y/y on Q4'25 $88.5M). That is derived, not quoted.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,765,604 shares = 17.31% of float, 9.44 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (FINRA, published 2026-10-26), down 13.67% from 3,203,623 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/IBTA/short-interest). Earlier: 3.2M, 13.7% of float, 17.7 days, 2026-08-20 (equibles). A crowded short that was covering into the 2026-10-15 +10.15% session. Baseline: put skew +12.69 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.74 on only 151 contracts total, ATM spread 27% of mid, so the skew is a thin-chain signal. Event-implied move 23.05% against a 28.54% median historical reaction. Spot $49.50 is at the 52-week high, +19.7% over 20 days and +157% off the 52-week low.

findings.finding: Ibotta has beaten the TOP of its own quarterly revenue guide in each of the last three reported quarters: Q4'25 $88.5M vs $80-85M guide (+4.1% over the top), Q1'26 $82.5M vs $78-82M (+0.6%), Q2'26 $88.9M vs $82-86M (+3.4%). Repeating that against the Q3 guide of $86-90M gives roughly $90.5-93M, i.e. +2-5% against the $88.4-88.6M consensus, which sits at the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported-quarter beat alone has not decided the reaction. Q1'26 beat the top of its guide and the stock moved -0.59%. Q4'25 beat the top and moved +28.54%, and Q2'26 beat the top and moved +51.91%; both came with guides that cleared the bar. So the beat pays only through the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($88.4-88.6M vs $88M) despite three straight beats over the top. If the street had priced the pattern, published estimates would sit near the top of the range or above it. A whisper above the top is likely embedded in a stock that is up 74% since the last print, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Q4'25 figures from the Q4 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260225755258/en/Ibotta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results); Q1'26 from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026031279/earningsrelease33126.htm. All three are company documents, so the pattern is one firm's guiding habit, not an independent series.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the line this name trades on, and the operating drivers point to a Q4 guide at or above the ~$93.4M implied consensus (+5.5% y/y). In Q2, third-party publisher redemptions grew +27% and IPN redeemers +21% (20.9M), and redemption revenue +10%. Uber (live Q2, 'ramp in the coming months'), Giant Eagle (live after Q2) and 7-Eleven/7NOW/Speedway (11,500+ stores, 100M+ loyalty members, go-live 'in the fall') all add publisher supply for Q4 that was not in Q2's base. Against that, management guides conservatively: Q2's actual was 5.8% above its guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises drive this stock. The raised Q3 guide (midpoint $88M against a prior consensus of about $85.9M) came with +51.91%. Q4'25 with a Q1'26 guide of -5% y/y that cleared fears: +28.54%. Q3'25: -23.68%. Q2'25 (2025-08-13): -30.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's FY2026 revenue of $353.35M implies only +5.5% y/y for Q4, below the +10% redemption-revenue growth already printed in Q2 and before three new publishers ramp. If the market agreed with the analysts, the stock would sit near the $36.57 average target, not at $49.50. So the price is likely above the published bar, and a guide merely in line with $93.4M may disappoint. That is why this is +1.0 on a wide band, not larger.
findings.independence: 7-Eleven go-live timing from trade press (https://www.cstoredive.com/news/7-eleven-announces-new-promotions-partnership/827087/, 2026-08); FY consensus from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ibta/forecast/. Q2 operating drivers share the Q2 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded and was covering into the print: 2.77M shares, 17.31% of float, 9.44 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 record date, down 13.67% from 3.20M on 2026-09-30. Average daily volume is only about 256k shares. With 3 Sell and 4 Hold ratings and a $36.50 average target, the short base is built on a fundamental-sceptic view that a beat plus guide-raise would force to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 print (+51.91%) and the Q4'25 print (+28.54%) both came off elevated short interest. The 2026-10-15 session (+10.15%, open $43.92 to close $48.93, no news found) coincides with the drop in shorts between the two October record dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the squeeze is a conditional mechanism that only fires on a good guide. The option market prices a symmetric 23% move with put skew, so it is paying for downside rather than for the squeeze. Some of the fuel has already been spent: shorts fell 13.7% in the second half of October.
findings.independence: Older equibles figure of 3.2M, 13.7% of float, 17.7 days, 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/ibta/shortinterest) shows the base was larger after Q2. Daily tape from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ibta/history/.

findings.finding: The expectations bar in the price is far above the published one. The stock is $49.50, up ~74% from the $28.49 after-hours price after the Q2 print, at a 52-week high, and above every published target: high $45 (Needham Buy), average $36.57, Goldman Sell with a target raised only to $35 on 2026-10-14, BofA Sell $22. The option market pays for downside (25-delta put skew +12.69 vol points).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26 beat the top of its guide and the stock went nowhere (-0.59%) after a run. Q2'25 (-30.28%) and Q3'25 (-23.68%) show what happens when the guide does not clear the bar.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this is the skew and the run-up restated, which the baseline carries. It is filed because the gap between the price and every analyst target ($49.50 vs $45 high) means the print has to beat a whisper, not the consensus. It is sized below what the skew alone implies because of the crowded short (finding 3).
findings.independence: Post-Q2 after-hours price $28.49 from the Q2 coverage (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3621954/ibotta-nyseibta-surprises-with-strong-q2-cy2026-stock-jumps-12); baseline skew and run-up. The analyst targets and the price path are different sources.

findings.finding: Insiders sold into the run: 10 Form 144 notices between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-30 plus Form 4s on 10-21 and 10-23. The CTO sold 25,018 shares on Oct 21-22 for about $1.25M (and 20,100 on Sep 10 at $40.04 under a 10b5-1 plan), and the CEO sold 5,030 at $41.57 on Oct 6. In total, 141,832 shares ($5.56M) were sold over 90 days; insiders own 20.92%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed link between insider sales and print reactions for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The filings are public but rarely read as a signal. Most sales run under pre-arranged 10b5-1 plans and are small against a ~$1.2B market cap, so the weak information content is why this is sized small, not neglect.

findings.finding: Instacart, an IPN partner (preferred third-party coupon provider since Aug 2024), reported Q3 2026 advertising and other revenue of $331M, +23% y/y, accelerating from +16% in Q2. CPG brand digital budgets on a grocery publisher that distributes Ibotta offers grew faster in Q3, the quarter Ibotta is about to report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of this peer read-through measured for IBTA.
findings.why_not_priced: The print landed after Ibotta last spoke (Aug 3), and the news was dominated by the DoorDash takeover announced alongside it, not by the CPG read-through. IBTA moved +2.00% and -1.58% on Oct 29-30, so no visible read-through. If it were priced, Q3 consensus would have moved off the $88M guide midpoint.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: Instacart's ad line is retail media (sponsored product), not pay-per-sale offers, and Ibotta's share of Instacart is not disclosed. Partner status from https://investors.ibotta.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/101/instacart-and-ibotta-join-forces-to-deliver-more-savings-for-customers.

findings.finding: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart for about $17B ($65/share, 26% premium over the 2026-10-22 close). Both are IPN publishers (Instacart since Aug 2024, DoorDash since Jan 2025, 115,000+ non-restaurant stores), so two of Ibotta's delivery-channel publishers will merge, concentrating publisher bargaining power over time. Close is expected at the end of 2027 or in H1 2028, so the in-window effect is only how management answers it on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IBTA closed -0.59% on 2026-10-23 and +0.14% on 10-26, so no visible reaction to the announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock did not react, so either the market sees no risk or has not connected it. Commercial terms are unaffected until close, which is why this is near zero.
findings.independence: Partner status for both from https://about.doordash.com/en-us/news/doordash-and-ibotta-partner and the Instacart release above. Instacart's 8-K (https://s25.q4cdn.com/251036341/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/CART-Q3-26-Earnings-Results-and-DoorDash-Acquisition-Press-Release.pdf) shares a document with finding 6.

findings.finding: Kraft Heinz, a large CPG advertiser, raised its planned 2026 investment by $100M to about $700M and guided to a Q3 promotional-timing headwind 'as investments increase', i.e. a CPG promo step-up in the quarter Ibotta reports.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since August and most likely in Ibotta's own Q3 guide, which was given two days earlier, so it is filed small. Kraft Heinz's own Q3 2026 actuals were not found.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that Ibotta has not confirmed. Kraft Heinz's promo dollars span trade, TPR and digital; Ibotta's share is unknown.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity: $67.3M of authorization remained at 2026-06-30 after $68.4M repurchased in H1 2026 (0.7M shares at an average $32.33 in Q2). Cash was $148.2M, with $99.0M undrawn on the revolver and $43.6M H1 operating cash flow. At the Q2 pace the authorization runs out around Q4, so a new or upsized authorization could come with the print. Against that, repurchases at $49.50 buy fewer shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A buyback was increased by $100M at an earlier print (date not confirmed); its isolated effect cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: The remaining authorization sits in the 10-Q, not in previews. A re-up would be new, but the buyback is a known feature of this name.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (finding 1's document) shows $23.0M bought in Q2.

findings.finding: The securities class action against Ibotta was dismissed in full, without prejudice, on 2026-08-03, with leave to amend by 2026-08-31. Its status after that date was not found, and the call may update it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: None. This shares the Q2 10-Q with finding 9.

findings.finding: Board change: director Thomas Lehrman resigned on 2026-09-22 with 'no disagreement' disclosed (he had sold 43.6% of his holding on Aug 11), and Tony Weisman joined as a Class I director on the Audit Committee.
findings.why_not_priced: It is fully public and carries no operating information.
findings.independence: The Lehrman sale is from the MarketBeat page cited in finding 5.

outside_window.finding: The DoorDash-Instacart combination closes at the end of 2027 or in H1 2028. Any change in either publisher's Ibotta terms after close is outside this window.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive (beat habit, crowded short, partner ad acceleration) and cut against the +12.7 put skew, but agree with the run-up's momentum. The run-up has put the price above every published target, so the real bar is a whisper above consensus; that is why p_up sits at only 52 despite a positive findings sum.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6: the reported-quarter beat-habit finding was cut from +1.5 to +0.8. This name has not paid for beats without the guide (Q1'26 beat the top: -0.59%), and the finding lands just above a range the company already guided.
Lesson 7: the run-up/skew negative was cut from -2.0 to -1.5 and the insider-sale negative from -0.5 to -0.3, because of the 17.3%-of-float short at 9.4 days to cover.

Lesson 5: the Kraft Heinz proxy was cut from +0.4 to +0.3 (unconfirmed transmission, likely already in the guide); the Instacart proxy stays at +0.8 as a direct-counterparty print that landed after Ibotta last spoke.
Lesson 2: the litigation one-off was cut from +0.2 to +0.1 (below operating income, no path to the guide).
Lesson 8 / core 3b: abs_move_pct was raised from 25 to 26 (median historical reaction 28.5 against implied 23.05; reactions are guide-driven).
Added the board-change 8-K at 0.0 for breadth (searcher addendum); the guidance, short-interest, DoorDash and buyback findings were left unchanged.
